documents.title: Your documents
documents.subtitle: Keep your source records together and link them to your bookkeeping.
documents.accept: PDF or MT940 · up to 20 MB · up to 100 PDF pages
documents.capability: Digital PDF text and one EUR MT940 statement per file are supported. Scanned PDFs are stored for manual review; OCR and automatic invoice/VAT extraction are not enabled yet.
documents.emptyText: Add a source file to start building an evidence trail.
documents.textNote: Text is provided as evidence. No accounting entries are created automatically.
documents.noText: No readable text was found. Review the original and enter the figures manually.

review.title: Bookkeeping
review.subtitle: Record the business event first, then its payment. Each entry stays balanced.
review.invoiceHelp: Use the VAT amount from the invoice. Payment is recorded separately against receivables or payables.
review.journalHelp: Choose the debit and credit accounts. For corrections, add a reversing entry and explain the change.
review.bankHelp: Choose the other account before recording a movement. To settle a recorded invoice, use receivables or payables. Invoice-level matching and VAT reconciliation are not yet available.
review.noBank: Upload an MT940 file to review bank movements here.
review.amountHelp: Use a decimal point for amounts, for example 121.50. Negative corrections use reversed debit/credit accounts.

yearend.title: Year-end checks
yearend.subtitle: Capture the explanations and supporting details your reviewer will need.
yearend.notice: Saving notes marks an item as supplied, not verified. Automated schedule calculations and accountant sign-off are coming in a later milestone.
yearend.placeholder: Describe the balance, period and supporting documents…
yearend.openingHelp: Explain the opening position and how it agrees with last year. For a new business, confirm the starting capital and assets.
yearend.bankHelp: Confirm all accounts and periods are covered, and reconcile opening and closing balances.
yearend.salesHelp: Confirm invoices, refunds and cash/card sales are complete without double counting.
yearend.purchasesHelp: Confirm supplier invoices and business receipts are complete, including personally paid costs.
yearend.vatHelp: List submitted periods, corrections, payments and year-end outstanding amounts.
yearend.ownerHelp: Explain private transfers and distinguish them from revenue and expenses.
yearend.cutoffHelp: List unpaid invoices, accruals and prepaid expenses, including bills arriving after year-end.
yearend.comparativesHelp: Provide prior-year accounts and details supporting the opening balances. Comparative reporting is not implemented yet.
yearend.cashHelp: Provide the year-end cash count and explain its reconciliation to the cashbook.
yearend.stockHelp: List quantities, purchase costs and obsolete stock at year-end.
yearend.equipmentHelp: Provide historical costs, accumulated depreciation, additions, disposals and useful lives.
yearend.premisesHelp: Identify lease commitments, refundable deposits and payments covering future periods.
yearend.staffHelp: Provide reviewed payroll summaries and outstanding payroll obligations. No payroll is calculated here.
yearend.loansHelp: Reconcile opening principal, advances, repayments, interest and closing principal.

guide.title: Your first report, step by step
guide.intro: From Home, choose Start a new report or Open an existing report. Then follow these five steps. Your saved records are kept until you choose to open them.
guide.quickText: Follow the short guide from your first upload to a draft report.
guide.help: What do I do on this page?

business.title: Set up your business
business.text: From Home, choose Start a new report. Enter the company name, year and activity, then select Next: your records. Choose the relevant features and select Create report and add documents. To revise a saved company, choose Edit company information on Home.
business.tip: Not sure about the VAT method? Choose “Not sure yet” and ask your accountant. The reporting year cannot be changed after creating this workspace.

documents.title: Upload your records
documents.text: Choose one PDF or MT940 bank file, then select Upload and read. Repeat for your invoices, receipts, VAT submissions and bank statements for this reporting year.
documents.tip: Open an uploaded file to check the original and any extracted text. PDF uploads do not create bookkeeping entries. Scanned PDFs need manual entry for now; MT940 files create bank movements to review.

review.title: Record invoices and payments
review.text: Start with your opening balances. For each invoice, choose Sales invoice or Purchase invoice, enter its date, description, total including VAT and VAT amount, then link its document and record it.
review.tip: Review imported bank movements separately. For payment of an invoice already recorded, choose Trade receivables for a customer or Trade payables for a supplier. This avoids counting income or costs twice.

yearend.title: Complete the year-end checks
yearend.text: Work through the checklist. For each item, explain the balance and name the documents that support it, then save your note. Include unpaid invoices and private transfers.
yearend.tip: A saved note means information was supplied. It still needs checking, and does not change the figures in your report.

report.title: Review and save your draft
report.text: Check the outstanding items and totals. Choose English or Dutch for the report. Select Print / save PDF, then choose Save as PDF in your browser. Use Export journal CSV to share the entries.
report.tip: Ask your accountant to check the draft before using it. VAT reconciliation and tax filing are not automatic, and this app does not submit anything to the tax authority.

guide.prepareText: Invoices and receipts, VAT returns, complete bank statements, previous closing balances (or your starting capital), and details of unpaid bills, assets and loans.
guide.exampleText: You invoice a customer €121, including €21 VAT. Record a sales invoice for 121.00 and VAT of 21.00. When €121 arrives in your bank, record it against Trade receivables. Revenue stays €100.
guide.openingText: What the business owned and owed at the start of the year.
